svg.aria-label: Three strategies that target processing: changing splice site choice in the direction of including an exon or of skipping one, the difference between increasing the normal product and switching to a less bad one, spliceosome inhibition and stop codon readthrough, and the condition under which changing processing rather than the gene can work.
svg.text: Strategy 1 change the splice site choice — the most successful category
direction A: INCLUDE the exon
ex 7
hnRNP
an ASO covers the silencer, hnRNP cannot bind,
and exon 7 is included more often
nusinersen, risdiplam in spinal muscular atrophy
goal: MORE of the normal product
direction B: SKIP the exon
mutated
the exon with the mutation is skipped; the product is
shorter but in frame, so SOME function remains
eteplirsen class in Duchenne muscular dystrophy
goal: a LESS BAD product
Direction B works only if removing that exon still leaves the rest functional. It lowers severity; it does not restore.
Strategies 2 and 3
2 inhibit the spliceosome — selectivity is the challenge; SF3B1-mutant cells may be more vulnerable
3 stop codon readthrough — strictly translation, same logic; tried in CF and Duchenne
The shared principle
Fixing the gene is not the only route. Leave the gene alone and
change HOW IT IS PROCESSED to get a better product.
The condition: usable material must still be present in the cell.
